title: Privacy Policy
metaDescription: How HudhudNest collects, uses, shares and protects your personal data, and the choices and rights you have.

blocks.p: HudhudNest is a digital real-estate marketplace where people publish and browse property listings for sale, long-term rent and short stays, and contact one another about them. This Privacy Policy explains what personal data we collect when you use the HudhudNest website and apps (together, the "Platform"), why we collect it, who receives it, how long we keep it and what rights you have.
We describe only what the Platform actually does at the date shown above. This Policy is information for you; it does not ask for your consent, which we request separately where the law requires it.

The Platform is operated under the trading name {{CONTROLLER_NAME}} ("we", "us"), a digital real-estate marketplace at {{WEBSITE}} and in its apps. We decide the purposes and means of the processing of personal data described in this Policy, which makes us the "controller" to the extent that concept applies under the law that applies to you.
Correspondence address: {{CORRESPONDENCE_ADDRESS}}.

ul: Privacy and your data rights: {{PRIVACY_EMAIL}}
General support: {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}
Legal matters and notices: {{LEGAL_EMAIL}}
Reporting security vulnerabilities: {{SECURITY_EMAIL}}

blocks.p: We have not currently appointed a data protection officer or a representative in the European Union. If we appoint either, we will add their details to this section.

This Policy applies to visitors, registered users, advertisers (owners, agents and agencies) and anyone who contacts us. It does not cover third-party websites or services that the Platform links to or relies on; those are governed by their own policies (see sections 13 and 21).
Depending on how you use the Platform, you may give us:

ul: Account data: first and last name, email address and/or phone number, and a password (we store only a salted cryptographic hash of it, never the password itself).
Sign-in with Google or Apple: if you choose these, we receive your name, email address and, from Google, your public profile picture.
Profile data: an optional profile photo, biography and contact details you choose to add.
Listing data: descriptions, prices, address details, map coordinates, photos, documents and the contact details you choose to publish for property sales, rentals, short stays and investment projects.
Agency data: business and location details when you create or join an agency.
Activity data you create: favourites, saved searches, ratings and reviews, short-stay bookings and booking requests, property-valuation requests, and expressions of interest in investment projects.
Messages: the content of messages you send to other users through the Platform.
Contact form: name, email address, subject and message text.

Launch-page waitlist: your email address or WhatsApp number, your optional interest (buying, renting or short stays), the page language and the time of your consent. We use it only to tell you when the Platform launches. If you registered earlier through the old interest form, we may hold the name, phone number, city, type of user and notes you sent.
Newsletter (optional): your email address, your language and the record of your subscription request, confirmation and withdrawal (see section 19).
Plan selection: the subscription plan you choose and its status. We do not collect payment-card details in the Platform at this time.
IP address: used for security (detecting abuse and suspicious sign-ins), rate limiting and short-lived security logs. It is stored with session records and sign-in audit logs.
Session data: a refresh token (stored in your browser as one strictly necessary cookie, and as a hash on our servers) and a short-lived access token that keeps you signed in.
Technical and error logs: operational logs that may include request details and error information, used to keep the service running and to investigate faults.

Sharing and attribution events: when a listing is shared or opened through a tracked link, we record the listing, the type of event and the campaign parameters (UTM) of the link, and your user ID if you are signed in. We do not store your IP address or message content in these events.
Landing-page funnel events: aggregate events (for example that a form was viewed or submitted) tied to a random session identifier, not to your identity or IP address.

Account-linked activity events (if you are signed in): invite, reward and usage-milestone events, and at most one daily activity marker per account. We use them to run the invitation programme and to understand which features are used. The person who invited you sees aggregate counts only; administrators can see the events.

App error reports: when the app hits an unexpected error it sends a short report to our own server (not to an outside service) with the kind of error, the platform, the app version, the page (without query parameters), the error message and the first lines of the stack trace, after removing e-mail addresses, long numbers and tokens. It is not linked to your account, IP address or device identifier, is not stored in the database and stays in operational logs only.
Aggregate usage counters: on the server we count how many searches and listing shares happen, with no identifier or identity, for capacity planning and to improve search.
Your approximate current location, only if you press the "near me" search: your browser or device asks for permission first, and we use the coordinates only to run that search; we do not store them.

Hosting provider logs: when you open the website or use the API, our hosting providers' servers (section 13) process technical connection data such as your IP address, the time of the request, the requested address and the browser type, and keep it in their operational logs for a period each provider sets.

blocks.p: At the date of this Policy we do not use advertising trackers, third-party analytics or crash-reporting services, or device fingerprinting; the error reports and counters above are handled on our own servers. We do use two device-bound identifiers, described in section 9 (an anonymous visitor id kept in your browser's local storage) and in section 13 (a push-notification token, only if you switch notifications on). If that changes, we will update this Policy first.
Listings are public by nature. Anyone, including people without an account, can see them, and search engines can index them:

ul: Property data: type, price, area, description, features and availability.

Photos: stored with our image provider (section 13) and served through public links, so anyone who has the link can open the photo. Do not upload photos showing identifiable people, personal documents or vehicle number plates without a proper basis for doing so.
Location: the listing's location is shown on the map. When you create or edit a listing you can choose to hide the exact location, and only an approximate location is shown.
Personal data inside a listing: your display name and any contact details you choose to include become public. Do not include data you do not want published.

blocks.p: We may republish the public content of a listing (photo, title, price, general location and link) on HudhudNest's own channels on third-party social networks such as Telegram, Facebook and Instagram to promote it. These posts never include your phone number or email address. You can ask us to stop promoting your listing at {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}.

We use your listing content only to run the Platform and to promote that listing and the Platform, within the licence set out in the Terms of Service. We do not sell it or license it to others for their own purposes.

Because listings are public, others (search engines, other websites or individuals) may copy or republish them without our knowledge. We do not control this and are not responsible for how others use what they copied. If you find a copy of your listing or data published elsewhere without a right to do so, tell us and we will help where we can, for example by asking search engines to remove cached copies after the listing has been deleted from the Platform.

Messages between users are stored so that conversations can be delivered and shown to the participants. We do not read them as a matter of routine, but we may access them where necessary to investigate abuse, fraud or a violation of our Terms, to handle a complaint, or to comply with the law.

If you submit a property-valuation request or an office replies to one, your contact details are shared with the valuation office only after you give a separate, specific consent for that purpose, which you can withdraw.

We send service messages (for example account confirmation, password reset, security alerts, booking and message notifications) by email, in-app notification and, for verification codes, by text message or messaging app.
To protect accounts we apply rate limits, record sign-in events, may notify you of unusual activity, and may periodically ask you to re-verify your phone number.

When you register or sign in with a phone number, we send a one-time verification code (OTP) through the channel you select: SMS, Telegram or WhatsApp. The code is delivered by the corresponding provider (see section 13); we store only a hash of the code, which expires after a few minutes. Your phone number must be supplied to that provider so the message can be delivered.

When you set a password, we may check it against a database of known breached passwords using a privacy-preserving method: only the first five characters of a hash of the password are sent, never the password.
We reviewed the code of the website and the app on the date of this Policy and classify what is stored in your browser or on your device as follows:

ul: Strictly necessary (no consent needed): one HttpOnly cookie that holds the refresh token and keeps you signed in, a cross-site request forgery (CSRF) protection token, a marker in local storage that a session exists and which sign-in method you used last, and a temporary marker in session storage that stops the page from reloading repeatedly after an app update. We also store your choice in the consent prompt described below.

Preferences (no consent needed, because you ask for them): language, light or dark theme, currency, how translated titles are shown, the areas you searched last and a temporary copy of translated listing titles. They stay on your device.

First-party measurement (with consent where the law requires it): a random visitor identifier used to count a listing view only once, the campaign parameters (UTM) of a tracked link you opened, and the invitation code if you arrived through an invitation link. They are not sent to any third party and are not used for advertising. If you are in the European Union, the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, Switzerland or Türkiye, or we cannot tell your country, we store them on your device only after you consent; otherwise they stay in the page's memory until you close it. You can change your choice at any time in Settings.

Third-party analytics and marketing: we do not use any on the date of this Policy. The code contains an advertising module (Google AdSense/AdMob) that is switched off by default; we will not switch it on before updating this Policy and asking for your consent where required.

blocks.p: Map tiles are loaded directly in your browser from OpenStreetMap (section 13), which therefore receives your IP address. Page fonts are served from our own servers. You can clear stored data in your browser or device settings; some settings may then return to their defaults.

ul: To create and secure your account and to authenticate you.
To publish your listings and let users find and contact one another.
To deliver messages, bookings, notifications and service emails.
To operate search, favourites and saved searches, including location-based search when you ask for it.
To prevent fraud, abuse and security incidents, and to enforce our Terms.
To maintain, debug and improve the Platform.
To respond to your requests and to handle valuation, agency and investment features you use.
To promote public listings and the Platform, and to measure which links bring visitors (without advertising profiles).
To send the newsletter, only if you subscribed and confirmed your subscription (section 19).
To comply with legal obligations and to establish, exercise or defend legal claims.
To keep a record of the versions of the Terms and Privacy Policy you accepted and when.

blocks.p: Where a data protection law requires a legal basis, such as the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) for people within its scope, we rely on the following, each for its own activities:

ul: Performance of a contract (Art. 6(1)(b)): creating your account and signing you in, publishing and showing listings, messages, bookings, viewing and valuation requests, the plans you choose, and service emails.
Legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c)): keeping or disclosing data where the law requires it, and answering and documenting requests about your rights.

Legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f)): Platform security and the prevention of fraud and abuse, security logs, error reports and aggregate counters, republishing public listings on our channels, keeping evidence of consent, and defending legal claims. We balance these interests against your rights.

Consent (Art. 6(1)(a)): the newsletter and the waitlist, sharing your contact details with a valuation office, access to your location for "near me" search, push notifications, and first-party measurement where the law requires consent. You can withdraw consent at any time without affecting the lawfulness of processing before the withdrawal.

blocks.p: We do not use consent as a general basis for all processing, and we do not treat accepting the Terms of Service as consent to marketing.

Right to object: you may object at any time, on grounds relating to your particular situation, to processing based on legitimate interests. We will then stop unless we demonstrate compelling legitimate grounds that override your interests or the processing is needed for legal claims. You may object to direct marketing at any time and without giving reasons.
The exact legal basis for a given activity may differ under the law that applies in your country.
We do not sell your personal data. We share it only as follows:

ul: With other users and the public, as you direct, through your listings, profile and messages.
With service providers that process data on our behalf (section 13).
With agencies or valuation offices you choose to engage, within the scope of your request and consent.
With authorities, courts or other parties where required by law or to protect rights, safety and security.
In connection with a merger, acquisition or restructuring, subject to this Policy or notice to you.

blocks.p: We use the following providers, and each receives only what it needs for its role:

ul: Hosting and infrastructure: Render (the API), Supabase (the database and the launch-page waitlist), Netlify (the web app and website pages), and a cloud storage provider for encrypted backups.
Cloudinary: storing and delivering profile and listing images.
Resend: sending email (account confirmation, password reset, security alerts, newsletter subscription confirmation, and newsletter emails to people who confirmed their subscription).
SMS providers (such as Twilio, D7 Networks or Unimatrix, depending on the country and configuration): delivering verification codes by SMS.
Telegram and WhatsApp (Meta): delivering verification codes when you choose these channels.
Telegram, Facebook and Instagram (Meta): publishing the public content of listings on HudhudNest's channels, as described in section 6.
Google and Apple: sign-in if you choose it. Google Identity Services is loaded in your browser on the sign-in pages.
Google Firebase Cloud Messaging and Apple Push Notification Service: delivering push notifications, only if you turn them on.
OpenStreetMap (the OpenStreetMap Foundation's tile servers): map tiles; the tile server sees your IP address.
Have I Been Pwned: checking for leaked passwords using k-anonymity, see section 8.

Only when switched on: DeepL for machine translation of public listing text, and OpenStreetMap's Nominatim service for turning addresses into coordinates on our server. Both are switched off in the default configuration.

blocks.p: These providers process data under their own terms and policies. We will update this list before we add a provider that processes personal data for a new category of purposes.

Your data is processed in countries other than your own. Some of our providers, or their parent companies, have servers in the United States or in other countries outside the European Union, and data may be transferred to them from Syria or from your country.

Where the GDPR applies to such a transfer, it may only go to a country covered by an adequacy decision of the European Commission, or with appropriate safeguards such as the Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) together with a transfer impact assessment and supplementary measures where needed. We are verifying the mechanism that applies to each provider and recording it in an internal transfer register, and we will not describe any transfer as compliant before it has been verified.
You can ask for information about the safeguards that apply to your data, or a copy of them where the law allows, at {{PRIVACY_EMAIL}}.
We keep personal data only as long as needed for its purposes, then delete it or remove what links it to you. These are the periods our systems apply:

ul: Account and profile data: as long as the account exists. After a deletion request and the 30-day grace period, it is removed or de-identified when the deletion runs (section 18).

Listings: a listing expires according to the listing lifecycle and is deleted together with its photos 30 days later unless you renew it. Listings of a deleted account expire when the deletion runs and are deleted after the same period, except listings of an agency member, which pass to the agency owner.
Session tokens: until they expire (30 days at most) or you sign out; their records are deleted 30 days after expiry.
One-time verification codes: stored as a hash, valid for minutes, and deleted one day after expiry.
IP addresses in session records and contact messages: cleared after 90 days.
Security logs: sign-in events 90 days, administrative and other account events 365 days, extended only as far as needed while a security incident is investigated.
Operational and error logs: kept by the hosting provider for its own retention period; we do not store them in our database.
Contact form messages: deleted 12 months after they were read, and in any case 24 months after they arrived. Data from the old interest form: 12 months after it arrived.
Waitlist: deleted after the launch notice is sent, and in any case no later than 12 months after you signed up.

Newsletter: as long as your subscription is active. An unconfirmed request is deleted 30 days after the confirmation link expires. After you unsubscribe we keep the evidence of consent and withdrawal for three years, then delete the email address and keep only a cryptographic hash of it so that we never send it marketing again.
Records of your acceptance of the Terms and this Policy: for as long as the account exists, then as long as needed to prove rights and obligations until the applicable limitation periods end.
Push notification tokens: until you turn notifications off or delete your account.

Backups: encrypted and rotated on a schedule (every 48 hours, then daily for 30 days, weekly for 12 weeks and monthly for 12 months). Data deleted from our live systems remains in older backups until they expire, and we do not restore data from them to live systems without applying the deletion again.

blocks.p: We may keep specific data longer only where the law requires it, to establish or defend a claim in an existing or reasonably expected dispute, or to investigate fraud; in those cases we pause deletion for the data concerned only and only for as long as needed.

We use measures appropriate to the risk, including encryption in transit, hashed passwords and tokens, encryption at rest for certain sensitive fields such as phone numbers, access controls and rate limiting. No system is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security. Please keep your credentials confidential and tell us promptly at {{SECURITY_EMAIL}} if you suspect misuse.
Depending on where you live and to the extent the applicable law requires (including the GDPR for people within its scope), you may have the right to:

ul: Access your data and get a copy: your account settings offer a self-service export of your data in JSON format.
Correct inaccurate or incomplete data: you can edit most profile fields in your account.
Delete your data: from your account or through the account deletion page (section 18).
Restrict processing in the cases the law sets out.
Data portability: the self-service export gives you a file in a machine-readable format.
Object to processing based on legitimate interests, and to direct marketing at any time (section 11).
Withdraw your consent at any time, including unsubscribing from the newsletter from any email or in Settings.
Not be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing that has legal or similarly significant effects; we do not make such decisions (section 23).
Lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority (section 25).

blocks.p: To make a request, write to {{PRIVACY_EMAIL}}, preferably from the email address registered in your account, and say which right you want to exercise. To verify your identity we may ask you to confirm the request from your account or from that email address; we ask for identity documents only if we cannot verify you otherwise. We answer within one month of receiving the request, which may be extended by two further months for complex requests, in which case we tell you why. Requests are free unless they are manifestly unfounded or excessive.
Where laws such as the CCPA/CPRA apply, we do not sell personal data or share it for cross-context behavioural advertising, and you will not be treated less favourably for exercising your rights.

You can ask for your account to be deleted from your profile or through the [account deletion page](/account-deletion). The deletion runs after a 30-day grace period during which you can cancel it. When it runs:

ul: Profile: your name, photo, biography and contact information are erased, your email address and phone number are replaced with values that cannot be linked to you, Google or Apple sign-in links are removed, all sessions are revoked and your photo is deleted from the image provider.
Listings: they expire immediately and are deleted with their photos after 30 days. If you are an agency member, your listings pass to the agency owner so that enquiries about them remain possible.

Messages and reviews: they stay visible to the people in the conversation or the readers of the review, attributed to "Deleted user" and without your personal data, because deleting them would affect the other party's rights.
Push notification tokens: deleted.
Newsletter: your subscription is withdrawn and your email address is removed from it immediately; we keep only the evidence of withdrawal and a hash of the address (section 15).
Consent and security records: kept for the periods in section 15 to prove what you agreed to and to protect the Platform.
Financial records: if there were paid transactions, we keep what the applicable accounting or tax law requires.
Backups: your data remains in them until each backup expires, as set out in section 15.

blocks.p: If the account is subject to an ongoing dispute or a preservation request from a competent authority, we may postpone the deletion until that ends, and we will tell you unless the law prevents it.
The HudhudNest newsletter consists of optional emails about Platform news and new features, offers and plan promotions, and updates about the real-estate market on the Platform.

ul: Subscribing is entirely optional and is not a condition for creating an account or using any feature. The subscription checkbox is separate from accepting the Terms of Service and this Policy, and is not pre-ticked.
Double opt-in: after you ask to subscribe we send one confirmation email, and we send no marketing until you click the confirmation link. The link expires after 72 hours.

Service emails are not marketing: account confirmation, password reset, security alerts and booking and message notifications are sent as part of the service, and unsubscribing from the newsletter does not stop them.

Unsubscribing: every marketing email contains an unsubscribe link that works without signing in, and you can also unsubscribe in Settings or by writing to {{PRIVACY_EMAIL}}. It takes effect immediately and we send no marketing afterwards.

Evidence: we record when you asked to subscribe, confirmed and unsubscribed, through which interface, which version of this Policy was shown and in which language, without storing your IP address. We keep this evidence for the period in section 15.
We do not sell email addresses or share them with anyone for their own marketing. Emails are sent through our email provider Resend (section 13).

blocks.p: The launch-page waitlist is separate from the newsletter: we use it only to tell you when the Platform launches and we do not add you to the newsletter unless you subscribe yourself. To withdraw your waitlist consent, write to {{PRIVACY_EMAIL}}.
We do not send marketing to existing users just because they have an account. Where marketing is based on your consent, you can withdraw it at any time without affecting what happened before.

The Platform is intended for people aged 18 or over and is not directed to children. We do not knowingly collect personal data from anyone under 18. If you believe a child has given us personal data, contact us and we will take steps to delete it.

Listings and profiles may contain links to other websites or services. We do not control them and are not responsible for their content or privacy practices. Please read their policies before you provide data to them.

Anything you publish in a listing, review, profile or message may be seen, copied or used by others. Please do not post personal data about other people without a proper basis to do so. We may remove content that breaches our [Terms of Use](/terms-of-service) or the rights of others.

We do not use automated decision-making that produces legal or similarly significant effects on you, and we do not build advertising profiles. Search results and listing ordering are generated from your filters and listing attributes. Paid featured listings are shown first. To show the paid listings of your area first, the app can send up to three region identifiers with the list request: the region you chose as your home area in Settings (stored in your account), the regions you searched for last and the regions of your saved searches. The last searched regions stay on your device only, in local storage, and are deleted when you sign out; the server does not store a search history for this purpose and the identifiers are not combined with other data. Our systems also automatically apply rate limits and security checks to block abuse.

We may update this Policy. The version, publication date and effective date are shown at the top of this page, and we keep previous versions. For material changes we will notify you in the Platform or by email before they take effect, and where the law requires your consent we will ask for it explicitly; in those cases merely visiting the page or continuing to use the Platform will not count as consent. Editorial changes that do not change the meaning may be published without asking for new consent.
For any question about this Policy or your data: {{PRIVACY_EMAIL}}. Correspondence address: {{CORRESPONDENCE_ADDRESS}}.

You have the right to lodge a complaint with the data protection supervisory authority in the country where you live or work or where the alleged infringement took place, where such an authority exists and the law gives you that right. We ask that you contact us first so that we can try to resolve the matter.
